PullRequest.Title: sessions: add image previews to reference hovers and align all artifact type behavior better
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

Chat session references currently make image files difficult to identify without opening them, and reference behavior differs between the Agents window and editor Chat. This change adds on-demand image previews to reference hovers and aligns rich metadata, actions, layout, and lifecycle behavior across both surfaces.

The references list remains compact: visual detail and additional actions appear only in the existing hover or secondary panel.

## Changes

### Image reference previews

- Shows a bounded thumbnail and supporting path when an image-file reference is hovered or keyboard-selected.
- Reuses the attachment image-preview component, thumbnail cache, and workbench hover styling.
- Reads local, remote, and Agent Host resources through the file service on first hover, with a 20 MB safety limit.
- Keeps the path visible and shows a localized unavailable state when an image cannot be read, decoded, or previewed.
- Cancels obsolete reads and disposes object URLs when hovers or references leave their visible lifetime.
- Leaves produced image artifacts and generic URL resources on their existing behavior.

### Consistent reference cards and actions

- Uses the same rich GitHub card for issues, pull requests, and commits in the Agents window and editor Chat.
- Lazily resolves commit metadata and preserves the newest metadata when duplicate references are merged.
- Adds capability-gated removal actions to editor Chat and announces successful removal to screen readers; backend failures use the notification service.
- Adds the appropriate copy action for each resource type:
  - website URL
  - file path or relative path
  - generic resource URI
  - non-GitHub issue or pull-request URL
  - GitHub URL or commit hash
- Keeps row actions concise and shows only incremental actions in collection hover footers.

### Layout, theming, and accessibility

- Shares responsive location and action layouts across file, image, and GitHub hovers, including narrow viewports.
- Uses workbench theme colors for links and hover actions instead of browser-default anchor colors.
- Keeps row accessible names, path descriptions, list navigation, and focus behavior unchanged.
- Gives preview images localized alternative text without adding a tab stop.
- Supports keyboard access to hover links and actions, with Escape returning focus to the references list.

## How to test

1. Open an Agents window or editor Chat session containing an image-file reference, a regular file reference, a website, and GitHub issue, pull-request, and commit references.
2. Open the **References** list and move through its rows with the pointer and with Up/Down.
3. Verify that an image row shows a bounded preview with its path beneath it, while the list itself remains compact.
4. Verify that unreadable, invalid, and oversized images retain the path and show the unavailable state instead of a broken image.
5. Verify that issue, pull-request, and commit rows show the same rich metadata hierarchy in both chat surfaces.
6. Exercise copy and removal actions from singleton hovers and collection rows; verify collection footers do not duplicate actions already available on the row.
7. Tab through rich-hover links and actions, then press Escape and confirm focus returns to the references list.
8. Resize the window so the hover is narrow and confirm long locations, titles, metadata, and actions wrap without horizontal overflow.
9. Confirm the negative cases: non-image file and URL references do not receive image previews, and produced image artifacts retain their existing **Images Preview** affordance.

## Validation

- Client transpilation and type checking pass.
- Targeted unit tests cover image-hover rendering and cancellation, reference actions and removal, GitHub metadata resolution and retries, duplicate-reference metadata, subscription disposal, and stable hover lifetimes.
- Targeted linting and `git diff --check` pass.
- Dark and light component fixtures cover landscape and portrait previews, production reference toolbars, GitHub metadata cards, action footers, keyboard traversal, and narrow layouts.
- The PR's **Compile & Hygiene**, Electron unit, browser, remote, smoke, CodeQL, telemetry, and **Screenshots & Tests** checks pass on the current head.

Live GitHub authentication, backend removal persistence and failure handling, and unavailable or oversized image states are covered by implementation and automated tests rather than the fixture walkthrough.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed call, FileService ordering, and Agent Host provider implementation are directly traced. The only uncertainty is how often users hover unusually large image references, which affects severity prevalence rather than the mechanism.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Full file bytes, including Agent Host base64 IPC payloads and renderer buffers
Findings.PerformanceScaling: The work and peak allocation scale with the actual resource size rather than the advertised 20 MB limit; an arbitrarily large image can be transferred and materialized before rejection.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Excessive I/O and peak memory can stall or terminate the renderer when an oversized reference is hovered.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Image-file references had a path-only hover, so hovering them did not read or transfer the referenced file.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The new hover immediately calls IFileService.readFile with a size limit, but FileService starts its stat validation and provider read concurrently.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added line 140 introduces the first filesystem read on the reference-hover path and relies on `{ limits: { size: 20 MB } }` as the safety boundary, even though that API starts the underlying read before the size validation finishes.
Findings.Title: Check the image size before starting the preview read
Findings.Impact: Hovering an oversized local, remote, or Agent Host image can still read the complete file before showing “Image preview unavailable.” Agent Host is especially costly because its provider performs resourceRead(Base64), so the full remote payload is transferred and decoded despite the cap.
Findings.Evidence: IFileService.doReadFileStream starts validateReadFile() and readFileUnbuffered() in parallel when no etag is supplied. The unbuffered path calls provider.readFile(resource) before validateReadFileLimits completes, and the Agent Host provider's readFile calls connection.resourceRead(..., Base64) without a cancellation token. On validation failure FileService consumes the already-started stream, so the 20 MB option does not bound this transfer.
Findings.Recommendation: Resolve/stat the resource first, reject files above 20 MB, and only then start the cancellable read (or use a streaming provider path that enforces the byte limit before buffering).

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The per-reference construction path, subscription lifetime, queue behavior, and exact polling intervals are all directly established. Only the typical number of references per session is uncertain.
Findings.PerformanceResource: GitHub REST/GraphQL requests and API rate-limit budget
Findings.PerformanceScaling: For N distinct references, opening the session creates O(N) initial requests. Every open issue then polls once per minute; each open PR keeps core polling once per minute plus checks every 15 seconds while pending or every five minutes otherwise.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Sustained excess network traffic, rate-limit pressure, and lower GitHub request throughput while the reference pills remain mounted.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Agent Host reference pills were built from recorded session metadata and GitHub session state and created no per-reference GitHub subscriptions.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Building the pill sections now calls the resolver for every issue and PR. Each resolver entry is retained for the whole session and subscribes at `visible` priority, including checks for every PR, even when the collection is collapsed and no hover is shown.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added line 365 creates a long-lived visible subscription for each issue reached from the newly added per-entry resolver calls; the adjacent added PR path creates equivalent core/checks subscriptions. Before the diff `_buildReferenceSections` did not query GitHub.
Findings.Title: Subscribe to GitHub details only while the rich hover is active
Findings.Impact: A long-running session with several referenced issues/PRs continuously occupies the GitHub request queue just to keep hidden hover details current. The queue limits same-account concurrency to one, but it does not reduce request cardinality, so ten pending PR references can approach 3,600 checks/core polls per hour.
Findings.Evidence: The changed resolver subscribes issues at line 365 and PR core plus optional checks at lines 389-393, then explicitly refreshes both. GitHubQueryService polls open visible issues every 60 seconds; PullRequestResourceService polls visible open PR core every 60 seconds and pending checks every 15 seconds. The subscriptions are removed only when metadata drops the reference or the whole component is disposed.
Findings.Recommendation: Create and dispose these subscriptions with the expanded row/hover lifetime, using recorded metadata while collapsed. If row enrichment is required, use one-shot batched/background hydration and avoid retaining visible polling interests for hidden details.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The eager call path and absence of a limiter in GitHubApiClient are explicit. Exact user-visible delay depends on session commit count and network latency, but the unbounded burst mechanism is deterministic.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Concurrent GitHub HTTP requests, response objects, and API rate-limit budget
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Opening a session launches one request concurrently for every distinct commit target in the artifact/reference collections, so request count and in-flight work grow linearly with commit history.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: A network burst and rate-limit pressure can reduce throughput for other GitHub operations when large session histories are opened.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Commit pills used the recorded label/hash and did not issue GitHub requests when artifact/reference sections were observed.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: SessionGitHubCommitResolver starts getCommit immediately on first `get`; section construction calls `get` for every commit while the toolbar evaluates its sources, before a dropdown or hover is opened.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added line 419 introduces the per-commit HTTP request; the newly added section loop reaches it for each distinct commit during normal toolbar rendering. The base behavior had zero commit metadata requests.
Findings.Title: Bound or defer commit metadata requests
Findings.Impact: Opening an Agents session with many recorded commits sends all corresponding REST requests at once. GitHubApiClient forwards directly to IRequestService with caching disabled and has no request queue or concurrency limit on this path.
Findings.Evidence: sectionsFor iterates all filtered artifacts and calls commitResolver.get(...).read(reader); added line 419 immediately invokes GitHubService.getCommit. That service performs one `/repos/{owner}/{repo}/commits/{sha}` request, and GitHubApiClient contains no limiter/coalescing across distinct targets. ChatInputPills evaluates every source's hasData to render the toolbar, so this runs while the pill collection is collapsed.
Findings.Recommendation: Defer commit resolution until the relevant dropdown/hover is opened, or route collection hydration through a bounded shared request queue; retain the per-target cache for coalescing duplicate SHAs.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The managed-hover lifecycle and downstream read call are explicit. Provider-level caching may reduce disk cost for some schemes, but remote and Agent Host providers still cross their boundary on every invocation.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Filesystem reads, remote/Agent Host transfers, and full image byte buffers
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Cost grows with both image byte size and the number of times the user reopens the singleton reference hover; rapid reopenings can overlap provider reads that do not support cancellation.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Repeated preview latency, bandwidth consumption, and allocation/GC pressure.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: A singleton image reference displayed only its location, so reopening its hover performed no filesystem I/O.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The WeakMap caches only an element factory. ManagedHoverWidget invokes that factory on every show, and the factory creates a fresh preview whose initialization reads the full resource each time.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added line 76 changes the singleton image pill from a static location hover to a per-show factory that creates a new filesystem-backed preview.
Findings.Title: Reuse the loaded preview across hover reopenings
Findings.Impact: Repeatedly hovering the same remote image rereads up to 20 MB on every opening. The thumbnail LRU does not avoid this boundary call because its cache key and lookup are reached only after readFile has returned the bytes.
Findings.Evidence: ManagedHoverWidget.update calls `content.element(token)` for each show and cancels it on hide. Added line 76 constructs a new createChatPillImagePreview each invocation; that helper immediately calls fileService.readFile. The only shared cache is getOrCreateImageThumbnail in chatImagePreview.ts, downstream of the full read.
Findings.Recommendation: Cache/coalesce the completed preview data or thumbnail for the entry's visible lifetime, keyed by resource version and invalidated on file changes, so reopening does not reread unchanged bytes.

Scenarios.Scenario: Hover or keyboard-select an image-file reference in a singleton pill or references dropdown
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The preview cannot display until resource stat/read, byte buffering, image decode, canvas resize, blob creation, and image load complete. The location shell can render first, but preview completion is on the hover's critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve metadata and read the entire referenced image with a nominal 20 MB limit
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One resolve plus one read for each preview creation; singleton hover reopenings repeat both, and each newly traversed dropdown image starts its own pair.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Reference hovers showed only the path and performed zero file reads.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The preview remains busy until the read and decode complete. For oversized files, FileService starts the provider read in parallel with validation and consumes it after validation fails.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Agent Host resourceRead returning Base64 file content
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One full remote call per preview creation, with payload proportional to the complete file size rather than the 20 MB cap.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Hovering Agent Host image references did not request remote file content.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks preview completion and can continue after hover cancellation because the provider API receives no token.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Image byte size, decoded pixel dimensions, number of distinct image rows traversed, and number of times a singleton hover is reopened.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: There is no preview-level limiter. Distinct row hovers can start independent reads; closing cancels the FileService token, but unbuffered providers such as Agent Host receive no cancellation token for their already-started resourceRead call.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The 50-entry LRU coalesces thumbnail decoding only after the complete source bytes and etag have been read. It does not cache or coalesce FileService reads. Failed thumbnail decodes are evicted. Reopening a singleton hover creates a fresh preview and rereads unchanged bytes.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed read call, FileService stat/read ordering, provider cancellation behavior, and managed-hover recreation path are directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Typical referenced screenshots are small, but large generated images and repeated hover traversal are realistic; exact transfer latency depends on scheme and connection.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable: the safety cap does not bound actual reads, and singleton reopenings repeat the full boundary operation.

Scenarios.Scenario: Render Agent Host issue and pull-request reference pills and leave the session open
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Initial row rendering does not await GitHub, but rich labels/status and hover details depend on asynchronous hydration. Continued polling is off the immediate render critical path yet persists for the mounted session.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One initial request per distinct issue, then one per open issue about every 60 seconds.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Agent Host reference rows used recorded metadata and made no per-issue request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off initial paint, but supplies rich row/hover metadata and consumes the shared GitHub queue and API quota for the session lifetime.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: GitHub pull-request core and optional-checks refreshes
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two initial fragment requests per distinct PR; open core polls every 60 seconds and pending checks every 15 seconds, with a five-minute checks backstop otherwise.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Agent Host reference rows used stored title/state and did not subscribe to per-reference PR fragments.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off initial paint, but continuously occupies the shared GitHub queue and quota while collapsed.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Effective unique issue and pull-request URLs after dedupe; open-state lifetime and pending-check duration control repeated calls.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: GitHubRequestQueue allows at most four global, two per host, and one per account. This bounds active requests but serializes same-account fan-out into a queue; it does not reduce total polling cardinality.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Normalized resources are shared per ref. Subscriptions are retained until the reference leaves metadata or the whole component is disposed. Open issues/PRs remain live and poll; failures back off, while successful open resources continue cadence polling.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: subscription creation, lifetime, queue limits, and polling policies are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Many sessions have only a few references, but sessions aggregating several active PRs can sustain substantial polling; prevalence affects severity, not the established cadence.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable boundary fan-out because hidden hover metadata is retained at visible polling priority.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open an Agents-window session containing commit artifacts or references
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Pill rendering itself uses recorded labels immediately, so HTTP is asynchronous and off initial paint; authoritative commit labels and rich hover cards wait for the corresponding request.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One concurrent request per distinct commit target when sections are first observed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Commit pills used recorded label/hash and issued no metadata request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off initial pill paint but required for rich commit metadata; competes with other GitHub work and consumes API quota.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request per distinct Agent Host commit, deduplicated by normalized target and bounded by the shared queue.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Agent Host commit pills did not fetch commit metadata.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off initial paint; metadata waits for queued completion.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of distinct GitHub owner/repo/SHA targets across artifact and reference collections after resolver-key deduplication.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The Sessions GitHubApiClient path has no application-level limiter, so all distinct commit requests are initiated in the same section evaluation. The separate Agent Host implementation uses the shared GitHub queue and is bounded to one active request per account.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Successful values are cached per resolver/component lifetime and duplicate SHAs coalesce. Sessions-window failures clear the in-flight store and retry on later reevaluation; there is no persistent cross-component cache or negative cache.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: toolbar source evaluation reaches every section, resolver get starts each request synchronously, and GitHubApiClient has no limiter.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Commit count varies with session history. The Sessions-window burst is deterministic for all distinct commits, but contention severity depends on count and network latency.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable for the unbounded Sessions-window request burst; the separately queued Agent Host commit path is bounded and not independently reported.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open rich GitHub cards and invoke copy/remove actions
Scenarios.CriticalPath: DOM card construction and bounded markdown-to-plaintext conversion occur when hover content is requested. Copy is local; remove performs one backend operation only after an explicit user action.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One backend call per explicit removal activation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: This surface did not expose the removal action.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Only the invoked action waits; normal rendering and hovering do not.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One selected reference at a time; title and description processing are capped at 80 and 200 visible characters after conversion.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No automatic action concurrency. Each removal is user-triggered and awaited by its own command path.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Issue/PR hover DOM is cached per link in the Agent Host surface and removed when metadata drops the link. Commit hover DOM is recreated but bounded to the active hover.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material for performance; operations are explicitly user-paced.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional performance finding: DOM work is bounded and action boundaries are one-per-user-command.

Scenarios.Scenario: Show existing in-memory chat attachment image hovers after the shared helper refactor
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Thumbnail decode, resize, blob URL creation, and image load remain on the hover preview path, using bytes already held by the attachment.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Attachment image bytes/pixels and up to 50 cached thumbnails.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Concurrent decodes for distinct attachments remain possible; same-key decodes coalesce through the cached promise.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The existing bounded 50-entry positive thumbnail cache and failure eviction behavior were moved into the shared helper; object URLs are disposed with hover lifetime.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the helper implementation is substantially the previous code with shared styling/MIME handling.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No changed boundary or multiplicity was found for existing attachment hovers.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression on the existing attachment scenario.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all changed files. Reported four diff-introduced regressions: ineffective pre-read image size enforcement, repeated singleton-hover image reads, long-lived visible GitHub polling for collapsed Agent Host references, and uncapped Sessions-window commit hydration. No concrete regression was found in shared attachment decoding, bounded hover DOM construction, copy/removal actions, CSS, or action-footer rendering.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
